persons.name: Hamza bin Laden

mentions.quote: On September 14th, 2019, President Donald Trump announced that Hamza bin Laden was killed in a U.S. counterterrorism operation along the Afghanistan-Pakistan border... There was reports he was killed in 2017.
Not only has Trump said that, but Al Qaeda has also eulogized him... may God accept him, referring to his so-called martyrdom.

events.description: President Trump announces Hamza bin Laden killed in a US counterterrorism operation on the Afghanistan-Pakistan border; earlier reports put his death in 2017.
Guido (Transatlantic Intelligence Consortium) posts an AI-generated video claimed as proof Hamza bin Laden is alive in Afghanistan; Sarah Adams retweets it.
Roy Grindvis reveals on X that he posed as Guido's Afghan sources since Feb 2025 and fabricated the AI Hamza video.
US drone strike kills Zawahiri in a Taliban safe house in Kabul; al-Qaeda has never announced his death or a successor.
Multiple inconsistent reports (Pakistani military, intra-Taliban dispute, US strike, rival group) claim Hakimullah Mehsud killed; TTP never confirmed.
Attempted Times Square bombing; TTP video with Hakimullah Mehsud proves he is alive.
Hakimullah Mehsud later killed in a US drone strike.
Abdul Haq al-Turkistani reported dead (c.2012-14), TIP names new leader; he later resurfaces alive and resumes leadership.
Fake ISIS statement celebrating Zohran Mamdani's New York victory circulated and shared by Sarah Adams.

key_claims: Hamza bin Laden should be presumed dead (US announcement plus al-Qaeda eulogy) absent verifiable evidence; the Dec 2025 'proof of life' video was an AI fake planted by a hoaxer on the Transatlantic Intelligence Consortium.
Al-Qaeda has never announced Zawahiri's death or a successor, which fuels speculation about its leadership.

Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence; the Adams/TIC circle relies on 'trust me, bro' sourcing, possible circular reporting, and some Afghan sources who inflate threats hoping to draw the US back.
Claims that al-Qaeda, ISIS, Haqqanis and Taliban have merged into one organization are objectively false; AQ and IS fight in the Sahel, Afghanistan and Syria despite localized cooperation.
Al-Qaeda is objectively re-established in Afghanistan with UN-documented camps, madrassas, safe houses, a weapons depot and media center, and top leaders present.
Leaders reported dead (Hakimullah Mehsud 2009, Abdul Haq al-Turkistani c.2013) have resurfaced; death claims need bodies, DNA or group confirmation.
